newsitem.title: USA: US LPGs steady, propane seen bearish ahead.
newsitem.headline: US LPGs steady, propane seen bearish ahead.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were largely steady in moderate midday trade on Thursday although some players pointed to bearish sentiment ahead given good supply of Canadian material.
Government data late Wednesday showed Canadian propane stocks up about 33 percent for April to levels 157 percent above year-ago levels.
"Canada is swimming in propane and people are starting to wonder if we aren't going to be seeing it coming our way," said a Midwest trader.
In Conway, Kansas, spot propane stayed steady, with deals done at 36.25 cents a gallon. Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot material also stayed steady at 35.25 cents.
Meanwhile, Belvieu normal butane strengthened a quarter cent to put sellers at 41.00 cents a gallon. Conway material was done at 37.50 cents, unchanged from Wednesday.

Tight supplies of Midwest isobutane may see a bit of relief, but not much, in the beginning of June. A Canadian source said a 50,000 barrel batch of field butane will begin moving down the Cochin pipeline to the Midwest by the end of May.
"It's just a grain of sand in the hour glass," said a Midwest player, adding that the shipment may have more of an emotional impact on the market.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1631
